exposure: Mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Type of cesarean section (elective vs. non-elective)
outcome: Cardiorespiratory fitness (Watt-maximum achieved on a cycle ergometer test at conscription)
cohort: 339,451 singleton males born in Sweden between 1973 and 1987
finding: While males born by cesarean section had lower cardiorespiratory fitness at 18 years of age compared to those born vaginally, this association disappeared after adjusting for familial confounding.
mod_finding: Both elective and non-elective cesarean sections were associated with lower cardiorespiratory fitness in young adulthood compared to vaginal delivery, with elective cesarean section showing a stronger association.
